headline: AI LABS RACE
TO A **1979** PROOF
cover.hook_pick_reason: No reader-impact hook: the heise online article states no effect on ordinary readers' prices, tools or risks. The headline is a rivalry plus the hardest fact: Anthropic and OpenAI each published a paper within hours, on a problem open since 1979. It says 'race' and 'to a proof', so it does not imply the proofs are confirmed (slide 5 and the caption say expert confirmation is pending) and does not say AI beat mathematicians. slides.title: Two labs, two papers, hours apart
body: Anthropic and OpenAI each published a paper within a few hours, heise online reports. Both are said to **solve a math problem open since 1979**, known as VP ≠ VNP.

slides.title: 70 pages from a Claude model
body: Anthropic published a **70-page paper on November 23**. Its proof came from an internal Claude research model, the report says.

slides.title: 30 pages, and an earlier date
body: A few hours later, OpenAI presented a **30-page paper**. By its own publication history, the company reached the result **already on November 6**.

slides.title: Experts have not weighed in
body: Independent expert confirmation of both papers is **still pending**. So both results remain claims for now.

slides.title: Both shared Lean versions
body: Both companies published their proofs in **Lean**, a tool for machine-checking math proofs. Anthropic says its check passed in Lean and in nanoda, an independently built proof checker.

slides.title: A Riemann claim got checked
body: Last week, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis using Claude. Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative say it is **logically valid** and matches the formal statement.

facts.text: Anthropic and OpenAI published papers within a few hours that are said to solve a mathematical problem open since 1979. (Our translation of heise online.)
Anthropic published a 70-page paper on November 23; its proof comes from an internal Claude research model.
A few hours later, OpenAI presented a 30-page paper. According to its own publication history, the company reached the result already on November 6.
Independent expert confirmation of both papers is still pending.
Both companies published formalizations of their proofs in Lean, a tool for machine-checking mathematical proofs.
According to Anthropic, the check with Lean and the independently developed proof checker nanoda was successful.
Only last week, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis with the help of Claude.
Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative have since independently confirmed that the formal proof is logically valid and matches the formalized statement of the Riemann hypothesis.

Anthropic and OpenAI each published a paper within hours, both said to solve a math problem open since 1979.

heise online reports that neither result has independent expert confirmation yet, so these are claims, not settled proofs.

→ Anthropic: 70-page paper on Nov 23, proof from an internal Claude research model
→ OpenAI: 30-page paper hours later; by its own history it reached the result on Nov 6
→ Both shared Lean versions; Anthropic says its check passed in Lean and in nanoda
